title: Console walkthrough - usage analytics & cost breakdown
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Console usage analytics and per-route dashboards focused on per-model and per-route latency, token counts and cost breakdowns. Customer asked about dedicated capacity vs hosted, VPC data residency, KMS, and a benchmark for 99th pct latency. Agreed next steps: share pricing, SOC2 + security packet, schedule benchmark run and pilot proposal.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-20 14:00 UTC · Duration 48m · Meeting ID ff-2026-10-20-emerald-001
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Lina Rivera (Emerald - Head of ML), Tom Graves (Emerald - CTO), Priya Singh (Emerald - Platform Eng), Alex Cho (Emerald - SRE)

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, do we have video? i see a couple cameras, great. quick agenda — we'll do a 30-ish minute walkthrough of the console usage analytics and per-route cost breakdown, then leave time for q's and next steps. demo is focused on how you'd track per-route token usage, latency p99, and cost allocation across models and routes.
00:28 Tom Graves: sounds good. our quick context — we're piloting LLM features in our product and want to understand unit economics. mainly worried about unpredictable spend and p99 latency spikes.
00:40 Maya Chen: totally, that's what we hear a lot. dan will share the console and run through the per-route dashboards plus the cost breakdown views. i'll chime in on commercial items and next steps.
01:05 Daniel Ortiz: ok sharing screen — give me a sec. so this is the Redwood Console home page, you can see total tokens, requests, and top models over the past 30 days. the left nav has routes, models, costs, and alerts.
01:30 Daniel Ortiz: jumping into routes — we instrument every route with per-token counts, average latency, p50/p95/p99 and an inferred cost column. this is derived from model unit costs + infra mix for hosted vs dedicated. you'll see a toggle to view hosted-only, dedicated-only, or combined.
02:05 Priya Singh: sorry interrupt — how accurate is the inferred cost? we have different commit sizes and reserved pricing for on-prem.
02:14 Daniel Ortiz: good question; it's a model — you can input your committed capacity and effective hourly rate for dedicated nodes and the console will amortize that into a per-token rate. for hosted calls we use usage tier rates. it's configurable per account or per region.
02:45 Maya Chen: we also surface confidence bands — if you have unusual burst patterns the console flags routes with cost variance >20% week-over-week.
03:02 Lina Rivera: can i see a demo route? show us a product example, like the assistant route we talked about.
03:10 Daniel Ortiz: sure, selecting "assistant-chat-prod" — here's the timeline for the last 7 days, tokens per minute, and a breakdown by prompt vs completion tokens. notice the orange spikes around 10/12 — that's when prefix caching missed due to prompt variations.
03:38 Daniel Ortiz: click into the p99 panel — we provide a sample-call view to replay traces, including model version, token breakdown, KV cache hit/miss, and which kernel (fp16 int8) was used on the host.
04:05 Alex Cho: replay is useful — do you capture request/response payloads? security is important for us.
04:12 Daniel Ortiz: we capture metadata and token counts, but payloads are never stored in plaintext unless you opt-in for debug, and that's limited to pseudonymized or customer-controlled logging. for private deployments you can disable retention; logs are encrypted with your KMS.
04:40 Tom Graves: when you say KMS, we use an HSM-backed KMS in GCP. will that integrate?
04:50 Maya Chen: yes, we support customer-managed KMS and bring-your-own-key for Dedicated and Private. we have integrations for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSMs via KMIP.
05:12 Priya Singh: okay nice. show the per-rule cost allocation — we want to split costs across product lines.
05:20 Daniel Ortiz: under costs > allocation, you can tag routes with business-unit tags. here i have the cost allocation view: route groups, token totals, modeled cost, and an attribution share. you can export CSV or push to your billing data warehouse via S3/GCS connectors.
05:45 Lina Rivera: neat. how do you handle multi-model routing? we sometimes route short prompts to smaller models and fall back to larger ones.
05:55 Daniel Ortiz: console shows a routing chain per request — primary model, fallback model, and weighted routing. costs are attributed to the final fulfilled model but you can also view the routing-level breakdown. there's also a heatmap for conditional routing misses that increases cost.
06:25 Tom Graves: can you show an example of a cost optimization suggestion?
06:30 Daniel Ortiz: sure — under Optimize we run heuristics on routes and suggest batching, cache TTL changes, and quantization profiles. here's a suggestion: for assistant-chat-prod, enable batching for low-latency concurrent requests and use int8 quantization for the 13B model — predicted savings ~32% with p99 impact <10ms.
07:02 Priya Singh: is the predicted p99 impact measured or modeled?
07:06 Daniel Ortiz: modeled based on our runtime telemetry and previous deployments with similar traffic shapes. for customers we always recommend a small benchmark run to confirm.
07:20 Maya Chen: and that's part of the pilot — we can run a two-week pilot with a focused benchmark and give you a validated savings projection.
07:34 Lina Rivera: benchmark — what exactly would you run?
07:38 Daniel Ortiz: we'd run a mix of synthetic traffic based on your trace (we can ingest a sample trace) and real shadow traffic if you want. we measure throughput, p50/p95/p99 latencies, token/sec, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll also measure eviction/KV cache hit rates.
08:05 Alex Cho: what's the SLA for dedicated? p99 latency SLO?
08:12 Maya Chen: Dedicated has SLA-backed throughput and uptime. for p99 latency we publish targets per model family — for example, 13B on A100 class infrastructure we target ~80-120ms p99 in steady state, but that varies by prompt length. we can share published performance profiles.
08:38 Tom Graves: those numbers seem optimistic vs what we've seen in-house. we run on multi-tenant infra and p99 sometimes spikes to 400ms.
08:50 Daniel Ortiz: that's exactly why smart routing and prefix caching matter. also our kernel selection adapts to sequence length — we can show a trace where switching kernel for long-context reduced p99 by 120ms.
09:10 Lina Rivera: you mentioned security docs earlier — can you point to SOC2, ISO, and audit log samples?
09:18 Maya Chen: yes i'll send the security packet after the call — SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 summary, penetration test redacted reports, and sample audit logs.
09:30 Priya Singh: on RBAC, can we map to our internal SCIM groups and SSO?
09:36 Daniel Ortiz: yes, SSO with SAML/OIDC and SCIM provisioning supported. RBAC is role based and you can tie audit log entries to user identities.
09:50 Tom Graves: ok back to costs — show me a per-route cost trend for the last 90 days.
09:56 Daniel Ortiz: switching to 90-day view — you can see seasonality and sudden cost spikes. here's an auto-generated explanation for the 9/22 spike: a model rollout to a larger variant increased completion token length by 40% — Optimize flagged it as a quality regression and cost anomaly.
10:30 Lina Rivera: do you integrate with Datadog or our APM?
10:35 Daniel Ortiz: yes we have tracing hooks and can forward metrics to Datadog, Prometheus, or NewRelic. we also export OpenTelemetry spans for request-level tracing.
10:50 Alex Cho: any mention of regulatory/data residency? we need EU-only data residency for some routes.
10:55 Maya Chen: Private deployment is the solution; we can deploy a control plane in your VPC or on-prem image. routes can be pinned to region and not leave the EU.
11:12 Tom Graves: what's the onboarding time for Private? months?
11:17 Maya Chen: depends on scope — small pilot usually 4-6 weeks, larger enterprise with integrations and HSM can be longer.
11:30 Priya Singh: ok, i have a question on per-token attribution for fine-grained billing across product teams — can we tag at the prompt level?
11:40 Daniel Ortiz: yes, you can pass metadata per request and that becomes a first-class dimension in the console for filtering and allocation.
11:50 Lina Rivera: show the export to BigQuery — we want to pipe all call-level metadata for ML ops.
11:55 Daniel Ortiz: exports are available; here's a sample connector config to BigQuery with schema. we anonymize PII fields by default.
12:10 Tom Graves: are there any gotchas around quantized models and accuracy regressions?
12:18 Daniel Ortiz: the Optimize tab also logs quality regressions and ties them to evals and prompt sets. we recommend running a small eval suite when switching quantization or model variants.
12:35 Maya Chen: ok time check — about 15 minutes left, want to open to next steps and q's.
12:45 Lina Rivera: quick one — competitor question: how do you compare to OpenAI in terms of price predictability?
12:52 Maya Chen: OpenAI is simple for dev but less predictable at scale; Redwood's value is cost predictability via dedicated, committed pricing, plus fine-grained allocation and Optimize suggestions to lower unit costs.
13:15 Tom Graves: and pricing model — send us a sample pricing sheet for hosted and a sample commit for Dedicated.
13:22 Maya Chen: absolutely.
13:30 Maya Chen: let's recap next steps: we'll send pricing sheet, security packet, and a pilot proposal — and dan will follow up to schedule a benchmark run.
13:45 Daniel Ortiz: action items i noted — i'll ask for a 7-day sample trace, and we'll scope the benchmark workload.
14:00 Maya Chen: great thanks all — we'll follow up by Friday with materials.
14:05 Tom Graves: thanks, that was helpful.
14:12 Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription artifacts; some product names transcribed as "Optimize" and "Console" consistently though internal names may vary.
